# Feedinbox integration guide

Feedinbox is two features delivered by one embeddable script (widget.js):

1. Feedback widget: a floating button that opens a feedback form.
2. Why-Not-Buy: a one-question exit-intent card that appears when a visitor
   abandons a high-intent surface (pricing page, pricing modal, checkout)
   without buying. It asks "What stopped you?" and records the reason.

Both features are controlled by the project's dashboard settings. The same
script is used in every case. The only site code beyond the script is the
event calls, which are required only for Why-Not-Buy.

Docs page (human version): https://feedinbox.com/docs

## Step 1: Add the script (required for both features)

Paste this before the closing </body> tag. Replace YOUR_PROJECT_KEY with the
project key found in Dashboard > Project > Settings > Project Key.

    <script>window.feedinbox=window.feedinbox||function(){(window.feedinbox.q=window.feedinbox.q||[]).push(arguments)}</script>
    <script async src="https://feedinbox.com/widget.js" data-project-key="YOUR_PROJECT_KEY"></script>

The first line is a queue stub (same pattern as gtag.js). It ensures events
fired before widget.js finishes loading are not lost. Always include it.

### Next.js (App Router), in app/layout.tsx

    import Script from 'next/script'

    export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
      return (
        <html lang="en">
          <body>
            {children}
            <Script id="feedinbox-stub" strategy="beforeInteractive">
              {`window.feedinbox=window.feedinbox||function(){(window.feedinbox.q=window.feedinbox.q||[]).push(arguments)}`}
            </Script>
            <Script
              src="https://feedinbox.com/widget.js"
              data-project-key="YOUR_PROJECT_KEY"
              strategy="lazyOnload"
            />
          </body>
        </html>
      )
    }

### React (Vite / CRA)

Add both script tags to public/index.html before </body>, exactly as in Step 1.

### No-code platforms

Use the platform's custom-code slot with the Step 1 snippet:
- Webflow: Project Settings > Custom Code > Footer.
- Shopify: theme.liquid, before </body>.
- Framer: Site Settings > Custom Code > End of <body>.
- WordPress: an "insert headers and footers" plugin, footer slot.
- Google Tag Manager: a Custom HTML tag that fires on all pages.

## Step 2: Fire the events (required only for Why-Not-Buy)

From the site's own pricing / checkout code:

    // Fire when a visitor reaches a buying surface
    // (opens pricing modal, loads pricing page, starts checkout, clicks Upgrade)
    window.feedinbox('event', 'high_intent', { plan: 'pro' })

    // Fire when they leave that surface without buying (e.g. pricing modal
    // close handler). Shows the card immediately. RECOMMENDED: this is the
    // most accurate trigger and lets visitors read pricing undisturbed.
    window.feedinbox('event', 'abandoned')

    // Fire when they actually buy. Cancels the pending question so buyers
    // are never asked.
    window.feedinbox('event', 'converted')

Rules:
- Event names must match the dashboard config. Defaults: 'high_intent',
  'abandoned', and 'converted'. Pro users can rename them; use whatever the
  dashboard shows.
- The third argument (context) is optional metadata, e.g. { plan: 'pro' }.
  It is stored and shown tagged on each response. Pass useful commercial
  context (plan viewed, price, billing period) when available.
- After high_intent, the card shows on the FIRST of these signals (unless
  'converted' fires first):
  1. the 'abandoned' event (immediate; strongest signal),
  2. an automatic exit signal: the cursor leaving through the top of the
     viewport, or the tab being hidden (automatic signals are ignored for the
     first ~3 seconds after high_intent to avoid stray-mouse false fires),
  3. a fallback timer (delaySeconds, default 30) so visitors who go quiet
     without any exit signal still get asked. This timer can be switched off
     in the dashboard, in which case the card waits for a real exit signal and
     a visitor who is still reading is never interrupted. Note that touch
     devices have no cursor signal, so with the timer off mobile relies on the
     abandoned event or the tab being hidden.
- 'abandoned' also works standalone: if high_intent never fired, it arms and
  shows the card in one call (context can be passed on it directly).

### Where to fire high_intent

At the exact moment of intent. Examples:
- Pricing modal open handler.
- Pricing page mount / route load.
- Checkout start.
- Click on an "Upgrade" / "Buy" / "Subscribe" button.

React example:

    function PricingButton() {
      const openPricing = () => {
        setPricingOpen(true)
        window.feedinbox('event', 'high_intent', { plan: 'pro' })
      }
      return <button onClick={openPricing}>See pricing</button>
    }

### Where to fire abandoned

Fire it from an explicit user action that closes a buying surface:
- Pricing modal close button / backdrop click / Escape.
- Checkout back or cancel action.
- A "Maybe later" / "No thanks" button.

React example:

    function PricingModal({ onClose }) {
      const close = () => {
        onClose()
        window.feedinbox('event', 'abandoned')
      }
      // ...
    }

IMPORTANT: do NOT fire abandoned from a component unmount, useEffect cleanup,
onDestroy, router-leave hook, or beforeunload.

Two reasons:

1. React Strict Mode (on by default in Next.js dev) deliberately double-invokes
   effects: mount, unmount, mount. A cleanup-based abandoned therefore fires
   milliseconds after high_intent, and because abandoned is the strongest signal
   and has no dwell floor, the card appears instantly on arrival instead of
   waiting. The same misfire happens in production whenever a component
   remounts (a parent key change, a layout shift, a route-group re-render).

2. It is redundant. The widget already detects page-level exits on its own
   (cursor leaving through the viewport top, tab hidden), so navigating away or
   closing the tab is covered without any code from you.

Wrong:

    useEffect(() => {
      window.feedinbox('event', 'high_intent', { plan: 'pro' })
      return () => window.feedinbox('event', 'abandoned')  // fires on arrival
    }, [])

Right (fire high_intent on mount, let the widget handle the exit):

    useEffect(() => {
      window.feedinbox('event', 'high_intent', { plan: 'pro' })
    }, [])

### Where to fire converted

On the real success step, so people who paid are excluded:
- Payment success callback (Stripe/Dodo/etc. onSuccess).
- Thank-you / welcome page load.
- Subscription-created event echoed to the client.

    // On payment success:
    window.feedinbox('event', 'converted')

## Feature combinations

- Why-Not-Buy only: dashboard feedback button OFF, Why-Not-Buy ON. Needs event calls.
- Feedback only: feedback button ON, Why-Not-Buy OFF. No event calls needed.
- Both: both ON. Needs event calls.

Toggling features is done in the dashboard, not in code:
- Feedback button: Widget editor toggle.
- Why-Not-Buy: Why-Not-Buy tab > Configure toggle.
Both toggles are free, as is switching the fallback timer on or off.
Customizing the question/options/delay length/event names is a Pro feature.

## Behavior

- After high_intent, the card shows on the first exit signal: the abandoned
  event, the cursor leaving the viewport top, or the tab being hidden. If none
  fire, the fallback timer (delaySeconds, default 30) shows it anyway, unless
  that timer has been switched off in the dashboard. A converted event cancels
  everything.
- Once a visitor answers, converts, or dismisses the card, they are not asked
  again for that browser session.
- Responses appear in the dashboard (Why-Not-Buy tab), tagged with the context
  (e.g. plan) and country, plus a weekly summary email.

## Troubleshooting

- Card never appears: confirm Why-Not-Buy is enabled, the event names match
  the dashboard, and converted is not firing immediately. Also check whether
  it was already answered or dismissed this session (sessionStorage keys
  prefixed feedinbox_intent_).
- Card appears the instant the page loads: something is firing abandoned on
  arrival. The usual cause is an abandoned call in a useEffect cleanup or other
  unmount hook, which React Strict Mode triggers immediately on mount. Remove
  it; page-level exits are detected automatically. See "Where to fire
  abandoned".
- Card appears while the visitor is still reading: the fallback timer is too
  short. Raise the delay, or switch the timer off so the card only appears on a
  real exit signal.
- Buyers are being asked: the converted event is not firing. Fire it on the
  real success step.
- Nothing loads at all: verify the project key and that the script tag is
  present on the page. Keep the queue stub line.

## Verifying the install

After adding the code, open the pricing surface (fires high_intent), then
close it (fires abandoned) and confirm the card appears immediately. Or, with
only high_intent wired, move the cursor out through the top of the viewport
after ~3 seconds. Submit an answer and confirm it shows in the dashboard's
Why-Not-Buy tab. To re-test in the same tab, clear sessionStorage keys
starting with feedinbox_intent_.
